findings.element: .b-back .b-item — the compressed past rail, day state and the guest phone, once BEHIND YOU is opened
findings.problem: The ticks and day-counts run on the compressed elapsed scale while the titles run on reading rhythm, and nothing connects the two, so the mark column stops indexing the rows it measures. Driven at 390x844 with the past open: ticks sit at y 640, 668, 682, 696, 724, 738, 948, 1160 while their own titles sit at 650, 699, 748, 797, 846, 895, 958, 1170. 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' is 157px from its own mark; 'Final dress fitting', 'Send the invitations' and 'Menu tasting' end up with no number and no mark beside them at all, while 14/28/35/42 clump against 'Final guest numbers' and 56/63 against 'Choose the evening music'. Worse, 'The Orchard reserved' has its mark at 948 while 'Send the invitations' has its copy at 846 — a reader tracing left from a row lands on a neighbour's mark. This is the audience's phone on the morning of the wedding, one tap from the first screen, and both gates pass it: the ticks never overlap, so 'no two items on the measure collide' holds, and the scale really is its own, so 'the past runs at its own scale' holds.
findings.fix: Draw the correspondence. For every .b-item inside .b-back, render a 1px hairline leader at var(--fore-24) from the tick's centre across the gutter to that row's .b-copy — an L: horizontal from the rail to 12px short of the .b-copy left edge at the tick's y, then vertical to the copy's vertical centre, then a 12px stub into the copy. Position it absolutely inside the .b-item, which is already the containing block for both, and take the two y values from the tick and copy offsets render-b.js already computes when it places the compressed rail. Same treatment in the print variant.

findings.problem: The two-column grid exists only inside @media (min-width: 1280px), so at 1024, 1100, 1152 and 1279 the whole plan renders as the phone stack blown up to desk width. Driven at 1279x800: the rail sits at x=206, titles end at x=774, the field ends at 1230 — 456px, 37% of the page, is empty beside every single row, and a screenshot at scrollY 700 is a thin strip of type pinned to the left of an otherwise black screen. The stack also costs 371px of height (scrollHeight 2130 at 1280 becomes 2501 at 1279, a 17% jump across one pixel of window) and pushes the first moment's top to y=941 — measured identically at 1024x768, 1100x800, 1152x800 and 1279x800. At an 800px fold that is 141px below it, so an owner opening their plan on a 13-inch laptop sees the counter, the gap note and an empty rail, and not one moment. The behaviour gate checks the fold only at 390x844, and the config lists 1152 and 1279 as first-class viewports, so this band is shot but not designed.
findings.fix: Move the two-column breakpoint down. Change the @media (min-width: 1280px) block that sets [data-medium="full"] .b-two { grid-template-columns: 344px minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 56px } to @media (min-width: 1024px), with grid-template-columns: clamp(280px, 26vw, 344px) minmax(0, 1fr) and gap: clamp(32px, 4vw, 56px), and move .b-stick's sticky rule into the same block. Reduce [data-medium] .b-measure padding-left from 124px to clamp(84px, 9vw, 124px) so the day-count gutter shrinks with the column. At 1279 that puts the horizon and the measure side by side, brings the first moment back above an 800px fold, and closes the 456px dead band.

findings.element: .b-edit .b-input and .b-seg below 1280px — the docked editing sheet
findings.problem: Below 1280 the sheet is full-bleed and nothing inside it is capped, so every control inflates to the page. Measured while editing: .b-input renders 1221px wide at 1279, 1094 at 1152, 710 at 768 and 332 at 390 — a date field holding '25 July 2026' drawn 1221px across. The .b-seg plate does the same: its box measures 1221px at 1279 while its two buttons measure 70px and 72px, so the Shown/Hidden control is a bordered box holding 142px of buttons at its left end and 1079px of empty framed nothing to the right. 'Done' is 61px wide and 'Delete this moment' a bare left-hugging line under it, both stranded at the left of a 1255x557 slab that covers 70% of the viewport. Every object in that panel hugs one edge and no line has a right edge. The same panel at 1440 is 344px wide and reads correctly, which is the proof that nobody has opened it in the band.
findings.fix: Give the sheet a measure. In the @media (max-width: 1279px) block add .b-edit .b-input, .b-edit .b-stepBtns, .b-edit .b-editActs, .b-edit .b-undo, .b-edit .b-readout { max-width: 480px }, and set .b-seg { display: inline-flex; width: auto } so the segmented plate shrink-wraps its two buttons instead of spanning the sheet. Leave the sheet itself full-bleed — the docked edge is right; only its contents need the cap.

findings.problem: The panel reserves 88px at its top for the reversibility bar, but that bar is visibility:hidden until something has been undone, so in the resting owner-editing state the panel opens with an 89px band of nothing above 'WHAT IT IS' against 16px on the other three sides — computed padding is 88px / 16px / 16px / 16px, panel top at y=597, first ink at y=686. It reads as a mistake, not as a reserve. It also costs the panel its foot: at the flagship 1440x960 that same 88px puts .b-editActs ('Done') at y=1034 and 'Delete this moment' at y=1085, both below the 960px fold, so the owner opens an editor whose commit control is off screen and nothing says so. Reserving the band is right; reserving it at the top, where the panel makes its first impression, and spending it on silence, is not.
findings.fix: Move the reserve to the foot, where the bar already lives at narrow widths. Render .b-undo as the last child of .b-edit rather than the first, set .b-edit padding to 16px on all four sides plus padding-bottom: 88px, and change the absolute offsets on .b-edit .b-undo from top: 16px to bottom: 16px. The panel then opens on its first label, the bar still sits inside the panel and still never stands on the count, and Done and Delete rise 72px — back above the 960px fold at 1440.

findings.element: .b-todayRule — the single indigo mark in the product
findings.problem: b.css line 101 caps it at max-width: 344px, which is the width of the desk left column, so it terminates its column only at 1280 and above. Everywhere else it is an orphan dash: measured 96 to 440 inside a 96-to-1056 column at 1152 (616px short), 96 to 440 inside 96-to-672 at 768 (232px short), 106 to 450 inside 106-to-1174 at 1279 (724px short), and at 390 it runs 20 to 364 inside a 20-to-370 column — 6px short of the right margin that .b-who, .b-when, .b-sub, .b-todayLabel and .b-gapNote all hold exactly. The one accent in a three-colour system is the one object that does not line up, and on the phone it misses by an amount that reads as a rendering fault rather than a decision.
findings.fix: Delete max-width: 344px from .b-todayRule in b.css line 101. The rule then fills its grid cell, which is already exactly 344px in the >=1280 left column, so nothing moves at desk width, and at 390, 768, 1152 and 1279 it lands on the same right margin as every other line in the identity block.

biggestWin: The proportional measure is the real thing. The vertical distance between two moments IS the number of days between them, at one consistent scale I verified across the rail at 1440 and on the printed sheet, and it reads without a legend or a single extra word — it turns a list into an instrument. The A4 keepsake is where it lands best: the 79, the date, the folded past and the rail all sit on one sheet at award standard, and I would ship that page today. Two pieces of craft under it deserve naming: the count is optically kicked 7px left of its column (x=179 against a 186 column at 1440, 15 against 20 at 390) so the seven's sidebearing does not break the left edge, and the surface keeps its place to sub-pixel accuracy through a reflow that adds 371px of height — a title held at y=-95.7 before a 1440-to-1279 resize sat at y=-96.3 after it. That is the class of detail that separates a mock from a product.
